answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, with no stake backing two identities at once. Whether agents catalog ivory, price marble, or inspect a ledge, each must post the same bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake bidders must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month. The mechanism does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying them consume scarce capital instead of merely generating new keys.
